title: Model recognition from a presheaf interval and anodyne extensions
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a small ordinary category, $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(A^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Set})$, and $1$ its terminal presheaf. Let $I\in\mathcal P$ have sections $e_0,e_1:1\to I$ for which $\delta=(e_0,e_1):1\amalg1\to I$ is a monomorphism. Products, pushouts and colimits are those of presheaves. For maps $i:U\to V$ and $j:K\to L$ write $i\square j:(V\times K)\amalg_{U\times K}(U\times L)\to V\times L$. Let $\mathrm{An}$ be the weakly saturated closure of a small set of monomorphisms; weak saturation means closure under isomorphisms, pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. Assume $e_\varepsilon\square j\in\mathrm{An}$ for every monomorphism $j$ and $\varepsilon=0,1$, and $\delta\square i\in\mathrm{An}$ for every $i\in\mathrm{An}$. Say $Z$ is naive fibrant when $Z\to1$ has the right diagonal-lifting property against $\mathrm{An}$. A right lifting property means existence of a diagonal in each commutative square. Let $[K,Z]_I$ be $\operatorname{Hom}(K,Z)$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by pairs which are the two restrictions of a map $K\times I\to Z$. Let $W_I$ consist of those $u:K\to L$ inducing bijections $[L,Z]_I\to[K,Z]_I$ for every naive fibrant $Z$ in the input universe.

There is a cofibrantly generated model structure on $\mathcal P$ with monomorphisms as cofibrations, $W_I$ as weak equivalences, and fibrations the maps lifting against all monomorphisms in $W_I$. Its fibrant objects are exactly the naive fibrant objects, and every map in $\mathrm{An}$ is a trivial cofibration. Explicitly, $W_I$ contains isomorphisms, has two-out-of-three and is retract closed; the pairs (cofibrations, fibrations in $W_I$) and (cofibrations in $W_I$, fibrations) are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system has a factorization of every arrow and its two classes are exactly each other's left and right diagonal-lifting classes. Both systems are generated by small sets, and the constructions and factorizations stay in the input universe.

source.place: Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, July 30, 2026, Example 2.4.10 (product with an interval is an exact cylinder), Definition 2.4.11 (An0-An2), Definition 2.4.18 and Theorem 2.4.19, printed pp. 52-57; Proposition 2.4.25 (anodyne maps are weak equivalences), Remark 2.4.22 and Proposition 2.1.9 for functorial small-object factorizations. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. This generic theorem is proved in Section 2.4 before the construction of the Joyal model category, without a rigidification or Joyal input. No Stacks tag states this theorem.

proof.text: Put $C=\operatorname{Mono}(\mathcal P)$. The presheaf presentability leaf gives local finite presentability and all small colimits; all small limits are computed objectwise by the compatible-tuples construction in sets. Hom sets are small subsets of products of component function sets. There is a small generating family $B$ for $C$: take representatives of every inclusion $S\hookrightarrow Q$ with $Q$ a quotient of a representable. Quotients are coded by objectwise equivalence relations on the small sets of a representable and their subobjects by subsets, so these choices form a small set. To check generation, identify a monomorphism with $F\subseteq G$, well-order the set of all elements of $G$, and recursively adjoin the subpresheaf $Q\subseteq G$ generated by the next element. It is a quotient of the corresponding representable: at object $b$ its elements are the restrictions of the chosen element along arrows $b\to a$. If the current subpresheaf is $H$, the successor $H\to H\cup Q$ is objectwise the pushout of $H\cap Q\hookrightarrow Q$, a member of $B$ up to isomorphism. At limits take unions. At the end the union is $G$. Thus $C=\operatorname{wsat}(B)$; the reverse inclusion follows objectwise because pushouts, continuous unions and retracts preserve injections.

source.place: Example 2.1.11, second method (quotients of representables); explicit element filtration and small-set coding.

proof.text: Let $\Lambda$ be the small set whose weak saturation is $\mathrm{An}$. Apply the accessible small-object factorization theorem separately to $B$ and $\Lambda$, using Step 1. For either set $K$, put $L=\operatorname{wsat}(K)$ and $R=K^\square$. A map lifting against $K$ also lifts against $L$: pushouts restrict lifting squares, transfinite composites are covered by the transfinite-left-lifting leaf, and retracts by the lifting-closure leaf. Thus $R=L^\square$ and $L\subseteq{}^\square R$. The supplied factorization $f=pi$ has $i\in L,p\in R$. If $f$ lifts against $R$, lift in the square with top $i$, left $f$, right $p$, and bottom the identity; the diagonal $d$ satisfies $df=i,pd=1$, displaying $f$ as a retract of $i$. Hence $L={}^\square R$. We have obtained functorial weak factorization systems $(C,C^\square)$ and $(\mathrm{An},\mathrm{An}^\square)$, with small generating sets. Write $R_0=C^\square$ and $N=\mathrm{An}^\square$.

source.place: Corollary 2.1.10, Example 2.1.11 and Remark 2.4.22; lifting and retraction maps made explicit.

proof.text: For a naive fibrant $Z$, direct $I$-homotopy of maps $K\to Z$ is already an equivalence relation. Reflexivity is the constant homotopy. If $h:u\sim v$ and $k:u\sim w$, put $h,k$ on the two faces $I\times\{0,1\}\times K$ and the constant $u$ on $\{0\}\times I\times K$. These maps agree on the intersections. The inclusion of their union in $I\times I\times K$ is $e_0\square(\delta\times K)$, hence belongs to $\mathrm{An}$, and a filler into $Z$ restricts on $\{1\}\times I\times K$ to a homotopy $v\sim w$. Set $w=u$ for symmetry and then use symmetry for transitivity. Thus equality in $[K,Z]_I$ is witnessed by one homotopy.

Every $a:K\to L$ in $\mathrm{An}$ belongs to $W_I$. For each naive fibrant $Z$, maps $K\to Z$ extend across $a$, giving surjectivity on homotopy classes. If two extensions $f_0,f_1:L\to Z$ agree as classes on $K$, Step 3 gives a homotopy on $K$. Together with $f_0,f_1$ this defines a map from $(I\times K)\amalg_{\{0,1\}\times K}(\{0,1\}\times L)$ into $Z$. Its inclusion into $I\times L$ is $\delta\square a\in\mathrm{An}$, so a filler gives $f_0\sim f_1$. This is injectivity. Moreover the testing maps are functorial functions of homotopy classes, so identities and isomorphisms lie in $W_I$, bijections give two-out-of-three, and a retract of a testing bijection is a bijection. Thus $W_I$ is arrow-retract closed.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.25 and Remark 2.4.21; no model structure used.

proof.text: Every $p:X\to Y$ in $R_0$ belongs to $W_I$. Lifting against $\varnothing\hookrightarrow Y$ gives a section $s:Y\to X$. Lift the square with left map $\delta\times X:X\amalg X\hookrightarrow I\times X$, top $(sp,1_X)$ and bottom $p\operatorname{pr}_X$. Its diagonal is a homotopy $sp\sim1_X$ over $Y$, while $ps=1_Y$. Precomposition with $s$ is therefore an inverse to precomposition with $p$ on every interval-homotopy quotient. This works without fibrancy of $X$ or $Y$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.17; section and homotopy constructed directly.

proof.text: A monomorphism $i:K\to Z$ with naive fibrant codomain lies in $W_I$ if and only if it lies in $\mathrm{An}$. One direction is Step 4. For the other, factor $i=qj$ by the $\Lambda$ factorization of Step 2, where $j\in\mathrm{An}$ and $q\in N$. Since $i,j\in W_I$, two-out-of-three gives $q\in W_I$. The naive-fibration Whitehead lemma applies because the codomain $Z$ is naive fibrant, giving $q\in R_0$. As $i$ is monic, lift the square with top $j$, left $i$, right $q$, bottom $1_Z$. A diagonal $d$ has $di=j,qd=1_Z$, exhibiting $i$ as an arrow retract of $j$. Therefore $i\in\mathrm{An}$.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.29, applying Lemma 2.4.28 with its fibrant-codomain hypothesis checked.

proof.text: Put $D=C\cap W_I$, and let $N_f$ be those maps in $N$ whose codomain is naive fibrant. We prove $D={}^\square N_f$. For $i:K\to L$ in $D$, factor $L\to1$ using Step 2 as an anodyne $j:L\to L'$ followed by a naive fibration. Then $L'$ is naive fibrant and $ji$ is a monomorphism in $W_I$, hence is anodyne by Step 6. In a square from $i$ to $p:X\to Y$ in $N_f$, extend its bottom map $b:L\to Y$ to $b':L'\to Y$ across $j$, using naive fibrancy of $Y$. Lift against $ji\in\mathrm{An}$ and $p\in N$; restricting the filler to $L$ gives the desired diagonal. Conversely suppose $i\in{}^\square N_f$, without assuming that $i$ is monic. Choose $j:L\to L'$ as above and factor $ji=pk$ with $k\in\mathrm{An}$ and $p\in N$ by Step 2. Now $p\in N_f$; a diagonal $d:L\to\operatorname{cod}(k)$ in the square with top $k$ and bottom $j$ satisfies $di=k,pd=j$. Next lift against $j\in\mathrm{An}$ and $p\in N$ with top $d$ and bottom $1_{L'}$. This gives $r:L'\to\operatorname{cod}(k)$ with $rj=d,pr=1_{L'}$, hence $rji=k$. The arrow maps $(1_K,r):ji\to k$ and $(1_K,p):k\to ji$ exhibit $ji$ as a retract of $k$, so $ji$ is anodyne. Since $j$ is monic, monicity of $ji$ implies monicity of $i$. Since both $j$ and $ji$ are in $W_I$, two-out-of-three gives $i\in W_I$. This proves the equality.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.30, with the monicity and both arrow-retract maps spelled out.

proof.text: The equality $D={}^\square N_f$ makes $D$ weakly saturated. The lifting-closure leaf supplies identities, compositions, pushouts and arrow retracts, and the transfinite-left-lifting leaf supplies every small continuous transfinite composite, with right class $N_f$. Thus all closure assertions used below hold before any model structure is constructed.

Use the bounded-enlargement lemma to choose $\alpha>|\operatorname{Mor}(A)|$. Let $J$ contain representatives of all arrows $U\hookrightarrow V$ in $D$ with $|V|<\alpha$. This is a small set: code the sets $V(a)$ by subsets of a fixed small set of size $\alpha$, code restrictions by functions between those sets, and code $U$ by subsets. Certainly $\operatorname{wsat}(J)\subseteq D$ by Step 8. For the reverse inclusion identify $i$ with $X\subseteq Y$ in $D$, well-order all elements of $Y$, and build $H\subseteq Y$ starting at $X$. Inductively require $X\to H\in\operatorname{wsat}(J)$. Then $H\to Y\in D$, by Step 8 and two-out-of-three applied to $X\to H\to Y$. At the next element $y\in Y(a)$, its generated image $Q$ has size at most $|\operatorname{Mor}(A)|<\alpha$. Apply the bounded-enlargement lemma to $H\hookrightarrow Y$ and $Q\subseteq Y$; obtain $V\supseteq Q$ of size $<\alpha$ with $H\cap V\hookrightarrow V$ in $D$, hence isomorphic to a member of $J$. Its pushout is $H\hookrightarrow H\cup V$. Use this as successor and unions at limits. The inductive requirement holds by weak saturation, and the final union is $Y$. Therefore $D=\operatorname{wsat}(J)$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.39 from Lemma 2.4.38; explicit well-ordered construction in place of a maximal-subobject argument.

proof.text: Apply the accessible small-object factorization theorem to $J$, using Step 1. Repeating the lifting and retract calculation of Step 2 with $L=D=\operatorname{wsat}(J)$ proves that $(D,F)$, where $F=D^\square$, is a weak factorization system with a functorial factorization and small generating set $J$. Its calculation uses precisely the same pushout, transfinite and retract closure statements, now with right class $J^\square$.

source.place: Conclusion of the proof of Theorem 2.4.19; small-object argument with the set constructed in Lemma 2.4.39.

proof.text: We have $R_0=F\cap W_I$. Indeed $D\subseteq C$ gives $R_0\subseteq F$, and Step 5 gives $R_0\subseteq W_I$. Conversely, let $p:X\to Y$ lie in $F\cap W_I$. Factor it as $p=qj$ by the $B$ factorization of Step 2, with $j:X\to T$ monic and $q:T\to Y$ in $R_0\subseteq W_I$. Two-out-of-three gives $j\in D$. A lift against $j$ and $p$ in the square with top $1_X$ and bottom $q$ gives $d:T\to X$ satisfying $dj=1_X,pd=q$. The arrow maps $(j,1_Y):p\to q$ and $(d,1_Y):q\to p$ make $p$ a retract of $q$. The lifting-closure leaf makes $R_0$ retract closed, so $p\in R_0$.

The category has finite limits and colimits by Step 1, $W_I$ has two-out-of-three and retract closure by Step 4, and Steps 2, 10 and 11 give the two functorial weak factorization systems $(C,F\cap W_I)$ and $(C\cap W_I,F)$. These are the model-category axioms. Both generating sets $B,J$ are small. The fibrations are $F=(C\cap W_I)^\square$ by construction, exactly the fibrations asserted in the item, and $\mathrm{An}\subseteq D$ by Step 4.

source.place: Theorem 2.4.19 conclusion, checked from the two constructed weak factorization systems.

proof.text: Finally $Z$ is model-fibrant if and only if it is naive fibrant. If $Z\to1$ lies in $F$, it lifts against $D$ and hence against $\mathrm{An}\subseteq D$. Conversely if $Z\to1$ lies in $N$, its codomain $1$ is naive fibrant (all maps to $1$ have their unique diagonal). Thus $Z\to1$ is in $N_f$ and lifts against $D={}^\square N_f$ by Step 7, so is in $F$. All element sets, quotient and subset codes, well-orderings, ordinal unions, and the small-object factorizations above are in the input universe: in each application the ambient Hom sets and colimits are small relative to that universe by Step 1, and $B,\Lambda,J$ are small in it. No change to the testing universe is made.

source.place: Theorem 2.4.19, fibrant-object and universe assertions; all small-object applications are relative to the fixed universe.
